title: An Alphabet of Praise to God
overview: This chapter is an alphabet poem, each verse starting with the next Hebrew letter, that praises God as a great and kind King whose care reaches everything he made.

parts.label: A promise to praise (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: The writer, traditionally David, calls God "King" and promises to speak well of him every single day. "For ever and ever" suggests praise meant to last a whole lifetime and beyond.

parts.label: Stories passed down (vv. 3-7)
parts.note: God's greatness is too deep for anyone to measure, so the poem pictures older people telling younger ones what God has done. Here "righteousness" means God keeping faith with his promises, not just being strict.

parts.label: Kind and slow to anger (vv. 8-9)
parts.note: Verse 8 echoes almost word for word how God describes himself to Moses in Exodus 34. The poem stretches that kindness wide: God cares for everything he has made, not only one people.

parts.label: A kingdom that lasts (vv. 10-13)
parts.note: All creation and God's faithful people speak of his rule so that everyone may hear of it. The last line of verse 13 is missing from most Hebrew copies but appears in the Dead Sea Scrolls and early translations, and it fills a gap in the alphabet pattern.

parts.label: Lifting and feeding (vv. 14-16)
parts.note: This King's power shows up in caring for people who have fallen or are weighed down. The eyes of every creature look to God for food at the right time, and he opens his hand and satisfies them.

parts.label: Near to those who call (vv. 17-21)
parts.note: God is described as close to anyone who calls on him honestly, and as listening to those who revere and love him. The poem also says plainly that he will destroy the wicked, then ends where it began, inviting every living thing to praise.

think: What is something good you have experienced that you would want someone younger to hear about one day?
